findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electrical lines routing extensively through the interior of the site, with four transformer pads located outside the historic 5-foot perimeter electric easements shown on the 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat. The electrical system design requires new utility easement areas to cover interior line routing and transformer pad footprints. However, no easement exhibits, surveyor-sealed field notes, metes and bounds descriptions, or separate instrument dedication documents are evident in the site plan set or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report references Austin Energy review completed, but no coordination correspondence regarding easement dedications is included in the submittal. Facts.md notes (line 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' indicating unresolved easement status. The existing 5-foot electric easements from the 1975 plat are insufficient for this project's proposed interior electrical infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: The project is filing a site plan (SP-2025-0126C) without a concurrent new subdivision plat, making EL-7.1 (plat dedication) inapplicable. Therefore, any new easements must be dedicated by separate instrument per Code § 14-1-21. The visual analysis of Sheet 21 confirms that proposed electrical facilities extend well beyond the historic 5-foot perimeter easements and require additional easement areas. Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) and UCM § 1.16.0(3) mandate that metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor must be provided to Austin Energy for review. The absence of these documents constitutes a failure to meet the separate instrument dedication requirement. The fact that easements are merely noted as 'may be required at a later date' indicates the applicant has not yet submitted the required surveyor-sealed documentation.
findings.comment: Metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes not provided for new electric easement dedications required for interior electrical routing and transformer pad locations. Applicant must submit surveyor-executed field notes and metes and bounds descriptions for all proposed electric easement areas to Austin Energy for review and approval prior to recordation.

applicableAreas: All proposed and modified electric easement areas
findings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easement encumbrances is evident in the supplementary documents reviewed. The facts.md document identifies six existing easements of record (greenbelt access, drainage, wastewater, drainage, public utility, drainage) but does not indicate submission of a title document showing all encumbrances. The Project Review Form and Consolidated Site Plan Application do not reference submission of title documents to Austin Energy. Requirements per Land Development Engineering Review note that 'Current and proposed easements should be shown on all site plan sheets,' but no title commitment or ALTA survey is documented as submitted for Austin Energy review per UCM § 1.16.0(1).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) explicitly requires submission of 'a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey' showing all easement encumbrances to Austin Energy for review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. This documentation is mandatory for projects with proposed or modified electric easements. The absence of this title document from the submittal package represents non-compliance with a foundational requirement for easement coordination. While facts.md documents existing easements, that internal research document does not substitute for the formal title document that must be submitted to and reviewed by Austin Energy.
findings.comment: Title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey with certification showing all easement encumbrances not submitted to Austin Energy for review. Applicant must obtain and submit to Austin Energy a formal title document (title commitment, title policy, ALTA/ACSM survey, or Ownership/Encumbrance Report) certified to show all existing easements and encumbrances affecting the property.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies easement boundaries on the perimeter (5' P.U.E. on north, 15' Drainage and Wastewater easements on east), but does not depict the extent or boundaries of the electric easement areas needed for the interior electrical infrastructure. The proposed electrical lines routing through the interior of the site between buildings and along driveways are shown, but the easement boundaries required for these interior lines and for the four transformer pad locations are not clearly delineated on the sheet. The design shows electric lines in the interior but fails to show corresponding easement areas. UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that easements be shown on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) mandates that electric easements must be depicted on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities. Sheet 21 is the electrical design sheet and is the appropriate location to show these easements. While the perimeter easements are labeled, the interior routing of electrical infrastructure is not accompanied by corresponding easement delineations. The absence of easement boundaries for the interior electrical system leaves the extent and location of easement rights unclear. A complete site plan requires that all easement areas be clearly shown and labeled, allowing stakeholders and inspectors to understand the spatial scope of Austin Energy's rights and access requirements.
findings.comment: Electric easements not shown on site plan sheets for all interior Austin Energy facilities. Electric easements for the underground lines routing through the site interior and for all transformer pad locations must be clearly depicted on Sheet 21 (and other applicable sheets) with dimensions and boundaries.

applicableAreas: Northern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows multiple trees proposed directly on or immediately adjacent to the overhead electric (OHE) easement line on the southern property boundary. Visual analysis identified tree symbols plotted within and parallel to the dashed OHE line, indicating vegetation placement within the electric easement footprint. Additionally, trees are proposed at the northern property boundary where the 5-foot historic electric easement exists. The landscape plan contains irrigation notes but no reference to Austin Energy license agreements, Austin Energy coordination, or acknowledgment of requirements for landscaping within electric easement areas. No separate license agreement document is evident in supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings that might obstruct Austin Energy's access to facilities within electric easement areas. The visual evidence of trees plotted within the overhead electric easement boundaries triggers this requirement. The applicant cannot simply plant within easement areas; prior authorization is mandatory. The absence of (1) tree/landscape restrictions on the landscape plan, (2) a license agreement document, or (3) any acknowledgment of this requirement on either the landscape or general notes sheets indicates non-compliance. UCM § 1.10.10.3 further states that Austin Energy reserves the right to remove any obstruction without fault, and property owners are responsible for all costs.
findings.comment: License agreement not obtained from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping and trees proposed within electric easements. Multiple trees are plotted within or adjacent to electric easement boundaries on the southern and northern property lines. Prior to final approval, applicant must obtain a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement authorizing vegetation placement within the easement areas, or remove/relocate trees outside easement boundaries.
